messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: High error rate on inference-runtime (kv-cache + batching) for us-east-1. 5xx spike and tail latency increase. Affected service: redwood-inference-runtime-prod

maya: acked. I'm oncall. Looking at dashboards now — thanks for the ping.

elaine: I'm pulling traces and the kvcache hit ratio graphs. Initial glance shows kvcache evictions spiking right before errors.

samir: I see correlating spikes in small-batch queue length and a recent quantization rollout (canary) on model: rwd-13b-q4h. Could be interplay — quant change + batch packing path.

maya: 1) Is there an immediate mitigation we can apply to reduce customer impact? 2) Any customers on dedicated who need manual outreach?

jorge: Support intake: two paying customers reported degraded latency and intermittent 503s in last 10m. I've opened INC-4321 and flagged for SE outreach.

opsbot: Deployed: rollback patch to runtime-bin v2.14.7 -> v2.14.6 on us-east-1 failed on host pool A (error: image pull timeout).

maya: Ok, do not attempt more full rollbacks until we confirm compatibility. Samir — can you toggle kvcache bypass for the affected model group? That should reduce KV failures while we triage.

samir: Executing temporary kvcache bypass for model-group rwd-13b (route: rwd-13b-*) now. Command: `POST /admin/models/rwd-13b/kvcache/bypass?action=enable&duration=30m`

opsbot: kvcache bypass enabled for rwd-13b on us-east-1 (change-id: cz-9921).

elaine: After bypass, 5xx rate dropped ~60% and p95 latency returned to normal for the majority of requests. Still seeing small fraction of errors from burst batching buckets.

maya: Good. For the remaining tail, can we reduce max batch size for rwd-13b routes to avoid pathological packing with quantized kernels?

samir: Reducing `max_batch_tokens` from 2048 -> 1024 for rwd-13b routes in us-east-1. Applying via rollout config: `PATCH /admin/routes/rwd-13b/config` with `{"max_batch_tokens":1024}`.

opsbot: Route config rollout started (rollout-id: rl-1776). 10%->50%->100% staged. No errors reported in rollout logs.

maya: Monitor SLA and errors. Jorge, ping the two customers that reported issues with a brief status update and ETA for postmortem.

jorge: On it. Message sent: "We're seeing an infrastructure-level issue impacting latency/503s; mitigation applied, working on root cause, will share postmortem."

elaine: I captured traces showing failed KV get calls timed out at 150ms and caused retry storms into the batcher. Looks like an ethereal combination: increased eviction rate due to newer quant layer memory pattern, and batching code didn't backpressure correctly when KV latency rose.

maya: Summary for pager: 1) Enabled kvcache bypass for model group, 2) reduced max_batch_tokens, 3) aborted immediate rollback of runtime. Impact: partial customer-facing 503s and elevated p95 (20% customers affected transiently).

samir: Root cause hypothesis: quantized kernel variant for rwd-13b introduced atypical memory eviction behavior under heavy parallelism, which increased KV eviction and latency, feeding into batcher backpressure loop.

maya: We'll schedule a post-incident review. Proposed time: 2026-03-18 1500 UTC. Can everyone make that? If not, propose alternatives.

samir: I'm available. I'll prepare crash dump + canary diff and a small repro harness.

elaine: Can do. I'll prepare SLO/metrics timeline, and add suggested runbook steps to prevent cascade.

jorge: I'll add customer impact notes and outbound comms log.

maya: Action items captured here — create remediation tracking ticket and assign owners.

maya: ACTIONS (short-term, owner, due):
- Create remediation ticket with timeline + rollback/playbook: owner: samir, due: 2026-03-20.
- Add KV health metric + kvcache eviction alarm to prod: owner: elaine, due: 2026-03-19.
- Add canary gate for quantized kernel rollouts (automated perf smoke): owner: maya, due: 2026-03-25.
- Document emergency kvcache bypass and batch-size knob operations in runbook: owner: samir, due: 2026-03-19.
- Support customer follow-ups and postmortem summary: owner: jorge, due: 2026-03-18 (postmortem publish).

samir: I'll create ticket REM-7890 and link INC-4321, include the kv bypass change-id cz-9921 and rollout-id rl-1776.

opsbot: Created ticket REM-7890: "Investigate kv-cache + batching regression for rwd-13b after quant rollout". Linked: INC-4321, cz-9921, rl-1776.

maya: Great. For remediation plan longer-term: 1) Add memory pressure tests for quant kernel variants, 2) introduce batching backpressure guard (reject or throttle when KV latency > X ms), 3) consider ephemeral in-memory local caching for hot prefixes.

elaine: Note: we should also add automated alert that correlates KV eviction rate + batcher queue length to reduce detection time. I'll put that in REM-7890 tasks.

maya: Handoff note: I'm oncall for another 30m, then samir will take over for next 4 hours to drive remediation ticket scoping. If anything spikes, page channel `#eng-oncall` and escalate to platform lead.

samir: Acknowledged, taking post-pager ownership for remediation scoping.

maya: Thanks team — we'll cover the postmortem agenda at the scheduled slot. I'll post calendar invite and include SRE, Runtime, Support, and Product.

jorge: Once postmortem is ready, I'll prepare a short customer-facing summary and timeline.

incident-bot: Incident ticket INC-4321: status: mitigated -> monitoring. Next steps: postmortem scheduled, remediation ticket REM-7890 opened.

maya: Closing thread for active mitigation notes. We'll keep REM-7890 for tracking. If any regressions reappear, reopen pager. :thumbsup:"
